paragraphs: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Zeiruz, son of the father-in-law of Rabbi Meir.

He was Rabbi Meir’s student, as in [Chullin 6b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.6b.5). [Jerusalem Talmud Demai 2:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Demai.2.1.11) has a parallel to his testimony before Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi. Hyman describes the testimony as Rabbi Meir eating a vegetable leaf, after which Rabbi permitted Beit Shean. Hyman cites Shabbat 146a for another incident.
In the corresponding account, Yehoshua asks Rabbi, “Didn’t Rabbi Meir require a sin offering in a case like this?”[^1]

notes.text: The Bavli gives Rabbi Meir eating a leaf in Beit Shean; the Jerusalem Talmud gives him taking vegetables from a garden in the Sabbatical year. The cloak incident is at [Shabbat 147a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.147a.9), where Yehoshua asks a question and Rabbi then lowers his cloak.
